newsitem.title: USA: Brady debt surges after Moody's rates Ecuador B1.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt surges after Moody's rates Ecuador B1.

text.p: Emerging debt prices surged Thursday after Moody's Investors Service rated Ecuador's long-term foreign currency debt at B1, the same level as Argentina and Brazil.
Brady bonds soared on the news that Ecuador, a favorite high-yield play for investors, received a rating comparable to what had been considered stronger credits.
Ecuador's discount bonds ECDISC=RR stormed close to 3-1/2 points higher to 78, while PDI bonds ECPDI=RR jumped 3-5/8 to 70-7/8, and par bonds ECPARS=RR gained 1-3/4 points to 53-1/4.

"Whereas before Ecuador had traded at a significant premium to other countries, that premium is going to narrow significantly," said Tulio Vera, managing director at Bear Stearns. "It narrowed today, and will trade closer to the pack going forward."

The rating action left Wall Street divided, and analysts debated whether Ecuador should be seen at the same level as the two largest South American economies and above Peru, whose bonds traded more than 100 basis points tighter than Ecuador.
"The Argentine rating is probably a little low rather than Ecuador rating too high, said Amy Falls, head of sovereign research at Morgan Stanley.
Bear Stearns's Vera said, prior to Moody's inaugural rating, the emerging debt market had deemed Ecuador as a weaker credit than its newfound companions.
"This comes as a surprise to the market," Vera said. "To me Argentina is a superior credit in every respect."
Several analysts forecast that Moody's would soon upgrade Brazil and Argentina's credit standings, and Brady spreads tightened across the board in sympathy.
Brazilian "C" bonds BR8D14=RR gained 7/8 to 83-3/8, while Argentine FRBs ARFLC05=RR picked up 3/8 to 95-1/8, and Mexican discounts MXFLL19=RR surged 1-1/8 to 94-5/8.
The Brady market benefited from a stable day in U.S. Treasury securites, where the benchmark 30-year U.S. T-bond slipped 2/32 to yield 6.44 percent.
"There is a lot of cash out there, there is a lot money ready to be put to work, and having a very solid Treasury market is providing momuntum to the market," Falls said.
